macros.name: abs
macros.doc: The \abs command typesets the absolute value while properly handling spacing, unlike |. . . |.

macros.name: asympteq
macros.doc: The \asympteq macro is used to typeset the asymptotic equivalence.

macros.name: bigo
macros.doc: Asymptotic comparison operators (in Bachmann-Landau notation) are obtained with \bigO or \bigo and \lito commands.

macros.name: bigO
macros.doc: Asymptotic comparison operators (in Bachmann-Landau notation) are obtained with \bigO or \bigo and \lito commands.

macros.name: card
macros.doc: We define \card as an alias for \abs but, to prevent incompatibility, our definition is delayed until the beginning of the document, after checking whether \card is already defined.

macros.name: changecol
macros.doc: The \changecol macro is used to switch to the next column, and alignment within each column is achieved using the usual alignment markers & and \\.

macros.name: curl
macros.doc: By default, operators returning vectors, \grad and \curl (or its synonym \rot more commonly used in Europe), are written with an arrow on the top.

macros.name: dlim
macros.doc: To limit the display style effect to the affected symbol only, like the amsmath command \dfrac, we can use the following macros: \dlim, \dsum, \dprod, \dcup, \dcap.

macros.name: dprod
macros.doc: To limit the display style effect to the affected symbol only, like the amsmath command \dfrac, we can use the following macros: \dlim, \dsum, \dprod, \dcup, \dcap.

macros.name: ds
macros.doc: With in-line math mode, display style can be forced with \displaystyle or its alias \ds.

macros.name: dsum
macros.doc: To limit the display style effect to the affected symbol only, like the amsmath command \dfrac, we can use the following macros: \dlim, \dsum, \dprod, \dcup, \dcap.

macros.name: eqdef
macros.doc: equals by definition

macros.name: FT
macros.doc: The Fourier and Laplace transforms are typeset with \FT and \LT respectively, which are defined as operators, but typeset using \mathcal.

macros.name: grad
macros.doc: By default, operators returning vectors, \grad and \curl (or its synonym \rot more commonly used in Europe), are written with an arrow on the top.

macros.name: hvect
macros.doc: When vectors with arrows are typeset side by side, the arrows can be set up slightly higher using \hvect (which inserts a vertical phantom of ‘t’) to prevent inelegant effects.

macros.name: innerprod
macros.doc: The inner product is typeset with the two-argument macro \innerprod, which is a shortcut for \left\langle , \right\rangle, e.g. \innerprod{u}{v} yields ⟨u, v⟩.

macros.name: lfrac
macros.doc: The \lfrac macro behaves like \frac but with additional spacing around the arguments, making the corresponding fraction bar slightly longer.

macros.name: LT
macros.doc: The Fourier and Laplace transforms are typeset with \FT and \LT respectively, which are defined as operators, but typeset using \mathcal.

macros.name: MathNormal
macros.doc: With the inverse switch \MathNormal, you can apply the normal (italic) style on any comma-separated list of characters.

macros.name: mathset
macros.doc: By default, \mathset is an alias for \mathbf, but if you prefer doublestruck letters, you can simply use \renewcommand\mathset{\mathbb} (with local effect within an environment or a pair of curly braces).

macros.name: MathUp
macros.doc: For example, when \MathUp{e} is called, any subsequent occurrence of e will automatically be set in roman, without the need to type \e explicitly.

macros.name: probastyle
macros.doc: The \probastyle macro sets the appearance of \P, \E and \V.

macros.name: QED
macros.doc: end of proof

macros.name: specialgreeksdef
macros.doc: \specialgreeksdef takes key-value options to choose a Greek letter font without loading an entire package, thus without altering the other (italic) Greek letters.

macros.name: systemsep
macros.doc: The \systemsep length can be used to adjust the gap between the opening brace and the mathematical expressions.

macros.name: txt
macros.doc: The \txt macro, based on \text from the amstext package (loaded by amsmath), adds \quadspacing around the text.

envs.name: system
envs.doc: By default, a system is written like an array environment with only one column, left aligned.
